extracted.intended_audience: researchers preparing NIH R21 grant applications (investigators and institutional grants staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and assembling a complete NIH R21 (PHS 398 / SF424 R&R) application package, including required forms, project summary, specific aims, human subjects sections, biosketches, facilities/equipment, letters of support, and resource sharing plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA instructions for application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although this application demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed since the grantee applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules. NIAID posts new samples periodically: https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract (Description)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concise Project Summary that states background, the central hypothesis, preliminary data, the rationale, and the specific aims to be tested (e.g., aims to determine range of fetal to adult T cells and relationship to vaccine responses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Project Summary should frame the problem, articulate hypotheses, summarize preliminary data supporting feasibility, and clearly list the Specific Aims that the application proposes to address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative / Public Health Relevance Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Project Narrative / Public Health Relevance Statement explaining why the proposed exploratory studies are relevant to public health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state how the work may provide proof-of-concept, impact understanding of disease or vaccine responses, and potential downstream benefits to population health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear Specific Aims that enumerate the discrete, testable objectives of the project (e.g., Aim 1: determine normal range of fetal/adult T cells; Aim 2: determine relationship between high fetal/adult ratio and Th2 responses to vaccines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims should be concise, measurable, and directly tied to the hypotheses and Research Strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Research Strategy section that describes experimental design, preliminary data, methods, rationale, and how aims will be achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Research Strategy should justify feasibility and rigor of approaches, and show how results will address the Specific Aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects — Protection of Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: If human subjects are involved, provide the Protection of Human Subjects section describing risk/benefit, protections, consent processes, and IRB information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include IRB approval dates or status, human subjects assurance numbers, and explanations of protections to minimize risks to participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects — Women & Minorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Address inclusion (and analysis plans) for Women & Minorities in the human subjects sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how women and minority populations are included or justify exclusions, and discuss plans for recruitment and analysis by these groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects — Planned Enrollment Table
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Planned Enrollment Table detailing numbers, demographics, and recruitment targets for human subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply numeric enrollment plans and rationale to support statistical/feasibility claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects — Children
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, include a Children section describing inclusion, protections, and special considerations for pediatric participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address consent/assent and pediatric-specific safeguards per NIH policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe available Facilities & Other Resources (Laboratory, Clinical, Animal if applicable, Computer, Office, and Other support services) that will support the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specifics: laboratory space, specialized multi-user instruments (e.g., FACSAria cell sorter, BD LSRII), BSL containment, clinical research center capacity, core labs, statistical consultation, regulatory support, computer/network resources, office/administrative support, and how these will be used for the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: List major Equipment available to the project, including make/model, capabilities, and location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify specialized or high-value instruments (e.g., 4-laser, 19-parameter BD FACSAria cell sorter; BD LSRII flow analyzers; confocal microscopes; DNA sequencers; ultracentrifuges) and note whether equipment is in-lab or in adjacent equipment rooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch (Biosketch) format and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Biographical Sketch for each key person following PHS 398 format, with required sections: A. Personal Statement; B. Positions and Honors; C. Selected Peer-reviewed Publications; D. Research Support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DO NOT EXCEED FOUR PAGES per biosketch. Include education/training (institution, degree, years, field), a personal statement linking the person's experience to the proposed work, positions and honors, selected publications, and current/previous research support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support / Collaboration Commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Letters of Support that document institutional or collaborator commitments (e.g., clinical sample collection, statistical support, access to specimens, core services).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should specify the nature of the support, responsibilities, available resources (e.g., number of cord blood specimens available, MTA terms), any associated fees/recharge mechanisms, and assurance that activities will be conducted under approved protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plan(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Resource Sharing Plan(s) describing how data, methods, and materials will be disseminated and shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State commitment to present data at conferences, publish promptly, and submit all final peer-reviewed manuscripts to PubMed Central; follow NIH Principles and Guidelines for sharing research resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF 424 (R&R) Face Page required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete SF 424 (R&R) face page fields: Type of Submission; Federal Identifier; Applicant Information (DUNS, EIN/TIN); Organizational legal name and address; Project/Descriptive Title; Proposed Project Start and End Dates; Congressional District; Project Director/PI contact info; Type of Application (New, Resubmission, Renewal, Continuation, Revision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurately populate identifiers (DUNS, EIN), contact information, and project dates and ensure the PD/PI and authorized organizational representative information are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Other Project Information items
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete Research & Related Other Project Information questions: Are Human Subjects Involved? Are Vertebrate Animals Used? Is proprietary/privileged information included? Environmental impact/exemptions? International activities? Attach required items (Project Summary, Project Narrative, Bibliography, Facilities, Equipment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer yes/no questions and provide attachments for Project Summary, Narrative, Bibliography & References Cited, Facilities, Equipment, and any other required attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Sites information
rubrics_metrics.description: List Project/Performance Site primary location(s) with full address, DUNS, and congressional district information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include organization name, street address, city, state, ZIP, country, and mark primary location; include additional locations as attachments if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated Project Funding and Certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide estimated federal and non-federal funding for the project and complete required certifications and assurances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorized representative must sign certifying the statements are true, complete and accurate and agree to comply with resulting award terms; warn about criminal/civil penalties for false statements (U.S. Code, Title 18, Section 1001).

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Checklist items
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete PHS 398 Checklist items such as Inventions and Patents disclosure (for renewals), Program Income, and Disclosure Permission Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to checklist items; if program income is anticipated, provide amounts and sources; indicate permission for government to disclose applicant contact/title details if application is not funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA and copyright / permitted use of posted sample applications
rubrics_metrics.description: NIAID notes that the text of the application is copyrighted and the awardee provided permission for NIAID to post the grant application and summary statement for educational purposes with conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material may be used for nonprofit educational purposes only, provided the material remains unchanged and the principal investigators, awardee organizations, and NIH NIAID are credited. FOIA requests may result in redactions to protect confidential information, reviewer comments, deliberations, and personal privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 508 Conformance and Accessibility note
rubrics_metrics.description: Note on Section 508 Conformance and Accessibility: the sample was reformatted to improve accessibility and a contact is provided for accessibility issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If trouble accessing content, contact the NIAID Office of Knowledge and Educational Resources at deaweb@niaid.nih.gov.
